## Codex Review (GPT-5.4)

This is a `new-component` PR that adds `DateField`, `TimeField`, and `DateTimeField` on top of a large shared temporal-field store, shared sections, and localization plumbing. The core interaction logic looks promising and the targeted type/unit/browser checks I ran passed, but the branch still has a few public-surface and docs-contract issues that would make the first consumer experience confusing.

### 1. Remaining Bugs / Issues
#### 1. 🟡 Root `children(section, index)` overstates how much custom rendering is actually supported (non-blocking)

In `packages/react/src/date-field/utils/useTemporalFieldRoot.tsx:35-39` and the generated API at `docs/reference/generated/date-field-root.json:80-83`, the `children` callback is described as arbitrary `ReactNode` rendering for each section. In practice the interaction model only stays intact if that callback still renders `DateField.Section` (or the `TimeField` / `DateTimeField` aliases), because only that part wires up `data-section-index`, section registration, and the section/separator event handlers that `TemporalFieldStore` relies on for selection and editing (`packages/react/src/date-field/section/DateFieldSection.tsx:38-57`, `packages/react/src/date-field/utils/TemporalFieldStore.ts:769-848`, `packages/react/src/date-field/utils/TemporalFieldStore.ts:1069-1090`). A consumer who tries to render a custom separator or custom section node directly from the root callback has no public way to satisfy that hidden contract.

This matters because the root callback is the most obvious customization hook in a brand-new public primitive, and it currently promises more flexibility than the implementation can actually honor. The safe customization path is really `SectionList` + `Section render={...}`, not arbitrary nodes from the root callback.

**Fix:** Either narrow/document the root callback as “render the provided section parts” instead of arbitrary nodes, or expose a public contract for custom section/separator rendering so consumers can opt in without depending on private wiring.

#### 2. 🟡 The DateField docs still teach an unlabeled pattern even though the implementation requires a real label association (non-blocking)

`docs/src/app/(docs)/react/components/date-field/page.mdx:16` says an accessible name can come from a `<label>` element, but the new demos still render a plain sibling `<label>` with no `htmlFor`, `id`, or `Field` wiring, for example `docs/src/app/(docs)/react/components/date-field/demos/hero/css-modules/index.tsx:8-14`. The field only upgrades sections to field-level `aria-labelledby` when a real association exists; otherwise it falls back to generic per-part labels like `Month` / `Day` (`packages/react/src/date-field/utils/selectors.ts:289-295`).

This matters because users will copy the docs examples first, and those examples currently contradict the page’s own accessibility guidance. The copied pattern produces a field with generic section labels instead of a meaningful field-level name.

**Fix:** Update the demos to use `Field.Root` / `Field.Label` or an explicit `id` + `htmlFor` association, and tighten the docs wording so it demonstrates a label pattern that actually wires through to the field.

#### 3. 🟡 The TimeField and DateTimeField API pages still point readers back to DateField for core parts (non-blocking)

The anatomy snippets on `docs/src/app/(docs)/react/components/time-field/page.mdx:22-30` and `docs/src/app/(docs)/react/components/date-time-field/page.mdx:22-30` correctly teach `TimeField.*` and `DateTimeField.*`, but the API reference blocks immediately below them still use `<Reference component="DateField" parts="Section, SectionList, Clear" />` (`docs/src/app/(docs)/react/components/time-field/page.mdx:35-36`, `docs/src/app/(docs)/react/components/date-time-field/page.mdx:35-36`).

This matters because it makes the public contract look inconsistent at exactly the point users check copy-pasteable API names. Even though the runtime aliases exist, the docs currently make it look like the new components only partially own their own parts.

**Fix:** Point those reference blocks at `TimeField` and `DateTimeField`, or add explicit prose that these parts are aliased and should still be consumed through the field-specific namespace.

### 2. Public API & Composition Assessment

| Area | Assessment | Notes |
|------|:----------:|-------|
| Shared part model | Good | `Root` / `SectionList` / `Section` / `Clear` is a sensible composition shape for a segmented field |
| Root render-function contract | Concern | The public `children(section, index)` type reads as arbitrary rendering, but safe customization still depends on the built-in section part |
| Separator customization story | Concern | Consumers can style separators via `Section`, but there is no public way to replace them with custom nodes while keeping interaction wiring intact |

### 3. Accessibility and Interaction Assessment

**Strengths:**
- The per-section labeling model is thoughtful once a real field label exists; the hidden per-part label spans in `useTemporalFieldRoot` are a reasonable way to get announcements like `Birthday Month`.
- The targeted interaction suites I ran passed in both JSDOM and Chromium for the date-only variant.

**Gaps:**
- I did not run assistive-technology validation, so I’m not treating the accessibility story as fully cleared from this pass.
- The new docs examples currently undercut the accessible-name contract by showing an unassociated `<label>` pattern.

### 4. State Management / Lifecycle Assessment

The shared `TemporalFieldStore` architecture is substantial but coherent. I didn’t find a new concrete lifecycle blocker in the remaining code pass after accounting for the fixes already discussed on the PR, and the shared root/store approach should keep the three field variants aligned better than separate implementations would.

### 5. Maintainability and Integration Concerns

**Strengths:**
- The three public fields reuse the same store and section primitives instead of forking behavior.
- The `Section render={...}` escape hatch gives a reasonable styling/custom-markup story once consumers stay within the provided part contract.

**Gaps:**
- The most prominent customization API on `Root` currently reads more flexible than it really is.
- The docs still describe `SectionList` as grouping sections into “a single element” (`docs/src/app/(docs)/react/components/date-field/page.mdx:49-50`), but `DateFieldSectionList` does not render its own element. That wording will confuse anyone expecting a real wrapper for layout or semantics.

### 7. Documentation / Examples Assessment

| Area | Status | Notes |
|------|:------:|-------|
| DateField accessible-name guidance | Concern | Page guidance is fine, but the demos do not actually implement the association they describe |
| TimeField / DateTimeField API references | Concern | Reference blocks still route core parts through `DateField` |
| SectionList explanation | Concern | Docs describe a wrapper element that the component does not render |

### 8. Test Coverage Assessment

| Validation | Status | Notes |
|-----------|:------:|-------|
| `pnpm typescript` | Passed | Full repo typecheck passed |
| `pnpm test:jsdom DateFieldRoot --no-watch` | Passed | 53 passed, 5 skipped |
| `pnpm test:chromium DateFieldRoot --no-watch` | Passed | 58 passed |
| `pnpm test:jsdom TimeFieldRoot --no-watch` | Passed | Included `TimeField` and `DateTimeField` root suites |
| `pnpm test:jsdom DateTimeFieldRoot --no-watch` | Passed | 43 passed, 2 skipped |

### Merge Confidence Score

| Dimension | Score | Notes |
|-----------|:-----:|-------|
| Core runtime/type checks | 4/5 | The targeted type and root test passes were clean |
| Public API clarity | 2/5 | The root render-function contract still overpromises customization freedom |
| Docs/examples accuracy | 2/5 | Multiple new docs paths still teach confusing or incorrect usage |
| Accessibility validation | 3/5 | Code inspection is decent, but docs contradict the accessible-name contract and I did not run AT validation |

Overall merge confidence is 3/5. I would tighten the `children(section, index)` contract and fix the new docs/examples before merging so the first consumer-facing story matches what the component actually supports.
